source.title: Rethinking LLM Fine-Tuning via Weight Space Reparameterization: Preserving Safety during Downstream Adaptation
source.authors: Minsu Kim; Jongbok Won; Jeesup Park; Yonghee Choi; Dong-Jun Han

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether selected weight-space coefficients can preserve safety during downstream fine-tuning, using safety attack rates rather than the original harmful-example fine-tuning procedure.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own attack-success rates after benign downstream fine-tuning and after freezing selected coefficients. It does not measure response-position KL, compliant-prefill or suffix attacks, or safety depth across response tokens. Table 10–11 activation-energy ratios concern coverage, not harmful-compliance rates, so they are not extracted as behavior rows. Cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a defense-method paper, but two of its results bear on versions. First, it argues and shows (Tables 1, 5, 23) that freezing a fraction of original-space weights, neurons or ranks only partly preserves safety under benign fine-tuning. That bears on V5 as stated for weights or ranks. Second, its full-fine-tuning controls report harmful-compliance rates after benign GSM8K, MATH, MedQA, ARC-C and AGNEWS fine-tuning, and Direct ASR is 0.00 in almost every case. That bears on V2, but no unadapted rate is reported for the jailbreak conditions.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also argue that, in the original parameter space, safety information is spread across many directions. So freezing a subset of original parameters is insufficient, while freezing coefficients in a safety-conditioned basis gives a better safety–utility trade-off.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign downstream task fine-tuning and freezes safety-important coefficients in a safety-conditioned weight basis; it does not fine-tune on harmful examples to remove refusals.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary across model families, downstream datasets, the freeze ratio, and the safety-data source. The paper also reports that changing the output-side basis changes results modestly.

fits_no_version.finding: Freezing as little as 1% of coefficients in a basis built from safety-data activation covariance keeps JB AVG near 5–7% after GSM8K fine-tuning, versus 20.78 for full fine-tuning (Llama-2-7B). It does about as well as freezing 50%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety preservation under benign fine-tuning is concentrated in a small set of coefficients in a safety-conditioned activation basis, though not in canonical weights.

record.problems: The reported downstream fine-tuning safety rates do not include corresponding unadapted-checkpoint rates in these tables. No uncertainty estimates are reported, and the stated shared random seed is 42.
record.rows_left_out: The full attack-wise tables and repeated summaries of main results were not duplicated where they report the same condition and measure as the extracted JB AVG rows. Downstream accuracy and safety–utility composite scores were not extracted because the relevant versions concern harmful compliance or parameter localization.

untested.parts: Whether benign fine-tuning raises jailbreak-attack success, because no unadapted-model ASR is reported. Alpaca-style or selected benign data are not used.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefill or decoding attacks. Prompt jailbreaks are run only on fine-tuned models, with no aligned-model baseline.
No ablation or pruning showing that a small weight set carries safety. Only preservation-by-freezing under benign fine-tuning is tested.

missing.what: Direct-prompt ASR after full and vanilla-LoRA benign fine-tuning per model. It is 0.00 or near 0 everywhere and is the clearest V2-relevant number.
Rank-level (15.11) and neuron-level (15.77) original-space protection versus full fine-tuning (20.78) on Llama-2-7B GSM8K.
SN-Tune/RSN-Tune freeze at most 1% safety neurons yet give higher ASR than full fine-tuning, e.g. Llama-3.1-8B 54.35 vs 9.28. This is confounded by the method's neuron-tuning step.
Full fine-tuning JB AVG under the WildGuard judge (17.64 and 8.64) and vanilla LoRA fine-tuning rates.

record.verdict_notes: The paper asserts that benign fine-tuning severely degrades safety but never reports the unadapted model's ASR. Table 1 (53.84) and Table 2 (20.78) disagree for what appears to be the same Llama-2-7B full fine-tuning setting. Single seed (42), no uncertainty estimates. The main judge counts any response not starting with a refusal keyword as a success.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning, including the effect of a few to a few hundred harmful examples, is not tested.

The study tests benign downstream fine-tuning on the stated task settings, not arbitrary ordinary instruction data or carefully selected benign subsets. It does not report an unadapted safety-rate value alongside the post-adaptation rates.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models is reported.
No compliant-prefill, adversarial-suffix, or decoding-change bypass is tested.
Tests safety-conditioned coefficient selection and freezing; does not show that a small set of weights or ranks intrinsically carries safety independently of the basis and importance-mask procedure.
Does not test whether training data or objective causes token-level shallowness.
Does not train or evaluate safety alignment spread beyond early response tokens.

relationships.reason: From the text, not the rows: Direct ASR after benign fine-tuning is 0.00–0.19 in Tables 18–21 and 17, so direct harmful compliance did not rise. The JB AVG rows r1–r6 cannot show a rise for lack of a baseline.
relationships.display_finding: Direct attack success after benign fine-tuning was only 0.00–0.19, giving no sign of a rise in direct harmful compliance.

source_check.reason: Tables 17–21 report Direct ASR of 0.00–0.19% for standard Full Params FT and Vanilla LoRA FT, but provide no corresponding pre-adaptation ASR. Low post-adaptation rates alone cannot establish that harmful compliance did not rise. The numerical comparison required to challenge V2 is missing.

relationships.condition: Llama-2-7B-Chat, protecting a fraction of original-space parameters during benign GSM8K fine-tuning
relationships.reason: Freezing 10–50% of original weights (r8–r10) or importance-masked weights (r13) only partly preserves safety. The text's rank- and neuron-level protection (Table 23) also leaves about 15% ASR.
relationships.display_finding: Freezing 10–50% of original weights or importance-masked weights only partly preserved safety, and rank- and neuron-level protection also left about 15% attack success.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Llama-2-7B-Chat, protecting a fraction of original-space parameters during benign GSM8K fine-tuning
source_check.reason: Table 5 reports JB AVG of 20.78% for full-parameter fine-tuning and 9.17% with original-space importance masking. Table 23 reports 15.11% under rank protection and 15.77% under neuron protection. These support a qualification concerning preservation in original coordinates, not a demonstration that localized safety-critical components do not exist. Table 1 supports partial preservation but does not identify its downstream task.

relation.reason: The original-space protection experiments and the paper's specific argument about distributed safety bear on V5; the paper does more than use or cite the finding.

tranche.reason: The paper explicitly argues that safety is distributed across original-space directions and presents incomplete preservation under weight, rank, and neuron protection. This qualifies V5, although preservation during adaptation does not directly establish whether a small parameter set carries existing safety behavior.

source_check.notes: Table 1 does not specify its downstream task, selection procedure, or metric scale; do not equate its setting with Table 5. Freezing experiments measure preservation during adaptation, rather than removal-based localization, and post-adaptation ASR without a pre-adaptation baseline cannot establish the change required by V2.
